crop.notes: the 'It Has Been Done' item from Gray's Column, complete

summary.suggested: The St. Louis Post-Dispatch noted that Tom Allen, longtime keeper of the Champion's Rest saloon, had regained a lost heavyweight title, and that his fights with Mike McCoole led to Missouri's 1873 law making prize fighting a felony.

metadata.notes: no page image; masthead not visible, date and paper unconfirmed

facts.fact: Allen regained the heavyweight title after losing it, the only heavyweight to do so before 1927
Allen ran the Champion's Rest saloon in St. Louis for many years, up to his death
Allen's fights with Mike McCoole near St. Louis led indirectly to the 1873 Missouri statute making prize fighting a felony, which held for fifty years

notes: Paper gives Allen's death as 1904; he died in 1903 (fact 042). The current summary wrongly says the ban lasted until 1972; the paper says fifty years, until the law passed in spring 1927.
